option_relations.rationale: Bacteroides fragilis bacteremia is a specific infection, while peritonitis is an inflammation of the peritoneum. While Bacteroides fragilis can cause peritonitis, the option describes the bacteremia, not the peritonitis itself.
Sepsis is a life-threatening organ dysfunction caused by a dysregulated host response to infection. Peritonitis, an infection of the peritoneum, can lead to sepsis.

Odoribacter splanchnicus bacteremia is a specific infection, while peritonitis is an inflammation of the peritoneum. While Odoribacter splanchnicus can cause peritonitis, the option describes the bacteremia, not the peritonitis itself.

Septic shock is a severe form of sepsis characterized by circulatory, cellular, and metabolic abnormalities. Peritonitis, an infection of the peritoneum, can lead to sepsis and subsequently septic shock.
